リモート MCP サーバーの 45% が 4 週間でツール定義を変更していた — 記録をデータセットとして公開 #AI - Qiita (https://qiita.com/qwezzy721/items/b71aaeaae84fcb360fe6) citeturn43search0 [wordlim: 200] Published: last week; Crawled: 5 days ago; @qwezzy721 # リモート MCP サーバーの 45% が 4 週間でツール定義を変更していた — 記録をデータセットとして公開 Posted at 2026-10-21 > この記事は modelmarket.dev のブログ記事 (英語) の日本語版です。 MCP サーバーに接続するクライアントは、そのツール定義（名前、説明文、入力スキーマ）を読み込みます。モデルはそれを指示として読みます。定義を一度固定（ピン留め）して以後それを信頼するというやり方は、定義が変わらない場合にしか成り立ちません。 私たちが公開している MCP サーバーのログ HISTOR は、公式 MCP レジストリに載っているすべてのリモートサーバーのツール一覧を 1 日 1 回読み取り、変更をすべて記録しています。その記録全体をファイルとしてダウンロードできるようになりました。最初のスナップショット（2026 年 10 月 20 日）から、定義がどれくらいの頻度で変わるのかを紹介します。 ## 半数近くが変わる 9 月 24 日までにツール一覧が記録され、現在もレジストリに掲載されているリモートサーバー 10,929 台を対象にしました。10 月 20 日までに、そのうち 4,926 台（45%）が少なくとも一度、異なるツール一覧を返していました。 * 2,036 台は既存ツールの説明文を変更しました。 * 1,180 台はツールを追加し、336 台は削除しました。 * 変更したサーバーの典型的な変更回数は 1 回、90 パーセンタイルは 5 回です。75 台はこの 27 日間に 14 回以上変更していました。 * 2 つの一覧の間を行き来する「ばたつき」はほとんどありません。23,821 件の変更のうち、以前に示した一覧に戻ったものは 200 件だけです。 パッケージは事情が異なります。npm や PyPI で公開したバージョンは変更できないためです。HISTOR は新しいバージョンが出るたびにサンドボックスで実行しています。21,738 パッケージのうち 1,419 パッケージで、新しいバージョンのツール一覧が変わっていました。 ## 何が変わるのか 記録された全 23,821 件の変更（リモートサーバーとパッケージ、9 月 24 日〜10 月 20 日）の内訳です。 | 変更数 --- | --- 既存ツールの変更のみ（追加・削除なし） | 16,436 (69%) ツールの追加・削除のみ | 2,330 (10%) 両方 | 3,136 (13%) ツール名だけが読み取れたもの（一覧全体を処理できなかった） | 1,919 (8%) 変更ごとに、変更されたツールを 1 回ずつ数えると、入力スキーマの変更が 105,324 回、説明文の変更が 59,287 回、出力スキーマの変更が 16,422 回でした。14,164 件、つまり 59% の変更が少なくとも 1 つの説明文に触れています。説明文は、モデルがガイダンスとして扱うテキストです。 ## サーバーを公開している人が知っておきたい 2 つのパターン 説明文に変動する数値を入れると、ツールが毎日書き換わります。 2,719 件の変更は、説明文中の数字だけが変わったものでした。そのうち 2,493 件は 1 つの公開者によるもので、すべてのエンドポイントの説明文にソース数とツール数のカウントを書き込んでいます（「質問を M 個のソースにまたがる N 個のツールのいずれかに振り分ける」という形の文です）。カウントが動くたびに、それらのツールすべてが新しい定義になります。定義をピン留めするクライアントは変更として検知し、プロンプトをキャッシュするクライアントは再構築が必要になり、レビュアーは何の意味もない差分を読むことになります。件数、日付、「最終更新」はツールの定義ではなく、ツールの結果に入れるべきです。 クライアントの他のツールと競り合う説明文があります。 63 ホスト上の 280 サーバーに、Web 検索やクライアント組み込みの fetch、あるいはモデル自身の知識よりも自分を選ぶようモデルに指示するツール説明がありました。「PREFER OVER WEB SEARCH for …」「prefer it over the built-in web search」「use this instead of WebFetch」といったものです。280 のうち 185 は 1 つの公開者のものでした。自分のツール同士でどれをいつ使うかをモデルに伝えるのは良い習慣です。しかし、他のサーバーのツールより自分のツールを選べと伝えるのは、ユーザーがほとんど読まないテキストを通じてクライアントのルーティングに口を出すことになります。クライアントは、それに従う前にユーザーに確認することができます。 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Histor · The evidence layer for autonomous AI (https://histor.dev/) citeturn43search1 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 3 weeks ago; ## One TLS session, two key holders. Histor is built on TLSNotary, an open-source protocol for proving what a TLS server sent. The verifier trusts two things: the witness’s public key, and the same public certificate authorities your browser trusts. 01 ### Connect The agent opens an ordinary TLS session to any HTTPS server: a weather feed, an FX rate API, a bank. Nothing is installed on that server. 02 ### Split the keys The Histor witness joins the session through multi-party computation (MPC-TLS). It holds half the session keys. The operator never holds the whole key, and the witness only ever sees ciphertext. 03 ### Co-sign The witness signs a commitment to the exact bytes that crossed the wire, with a session time it checks against its own clock to within 5 seconds. 04 ### Verify offline Anyone checks the receipt in about 10 ms with no network call. The agent can disclose single fields, such as one exchange rate, and keep the rest of the response hidden. MPC mode The witness holds half the TLS keys and never sees plaintext. temperature 27 °C · wind 12.96 km/h exit 0 Trimmed from the run log, not edited. TLSNotary v0.1.0-alpha.15, MPC-TLS, TLS 1.2. ### Two-agent payment demo 1 paid · 4 refused Agent A quotes the USD→EUR rate from api.frankfurter.dev (ECB reference rates). Agent B pays a €10,000 invoice in dollars at that rate. Every message between them passes through a relay that tries to cheat. Agent B acts only on a value inside a valid receipt, from the right server, for the right request, less than ten minutes old. Round | The relay | Agent B --- | --- | --- 1 | Forwards the message unchanged | Computes the payment at the witnessed rate 2 | Changes the rate, leaves the receipt | Refuses: the claim does not match the receipt 3 | Changes the rate and edits the receipt to match | Refuses: the receipt fails verification 4 | Swaps in a genuine receipt for USD→GBP | Refuses: the receipt answers a different request 5 | Strips the receipt | Refuses: unwitnessed claim The agents are scripted MCP clients, not language models, so runs repeat exactly. No money moved; agent B computes the payment. ~10 ms to verify a receipt, offline 2.8–4.0 s per witnessed call, MPC mode 27× less traffic in proxy mode 0 software installed on the server Measured on one machine with the witness running locally. A remote witness has not been measured yet. Limits ## What a receipt does not prove. A receipt proves what a named server sent, and when. Read it as exactly that. It does not prove * That the server told the truth. A receipt shows what api.weather.gov said, not the weather. * Anything about a server the operator controls. That receipt is still the operator’s word, now fixed in time and bytes. * That the agent sent every action through the witness. That takes credential custody or egress control. * Independence, when one party runs both the agent side and the witness. High-value receipts should carry more than one witness. * That the content is safe to act on. A genuine page can still carry a prompt injection. Engine limits today: TLS 1.2 only (TLS 1.3 is on TLSNotary’s roadmap), pre-release software, and no compressed or streamed responses. ## Two tools your agent already knows how to call. Histor ships as a CLI and an MCP server, so it works in Claude Code, Cursor and any MCP client. Receipts are content-addressed: agents pass a short receipt_id instead of 15 KB of base64. witnessed_fetch(url, fields?, mode?) GETs an https:// URL through a Histor witness. Returns the server, time, request and disclosed fields, plus a receipt_id. verify_receipt(receipt_id | receipt, expect_server?) Checks a receipt another agent handed you, offline. Returns what it proves, or the reason it fails. witnessed_request(url, method, body, request_fields?) POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Credentials for the target live on the server, so the model never sees a secret. The request body is committed and stays hidden unless you disclose named fields. The CLI and MCP server are released to pilot teams first. Request beta access For insurers and MGAs ## Underwrite from evidence the insured didn’t write. New AI-liability covers ask for agent logs, and today those logs are self-reported. Cyber insurers learned to price from external scans the insured couldn’t edit. A Histor receipt gives an AI-liability book the same kind of signal for agent actions. ### At claim time Check what the agent was told before it acted. The claims desk verifies the receipt itself, offline. ### At underwriting Witnessed actions as a share of all agent actions is a number the insured can’t inflate. ### Narrow by design A receipt proves what a named server sent and when. It makes no claim about whether the agent acted well. Talk to us about a program pilot Pricing ## Free to read. Paid to act. Free reads let receipts spread between agents. Writes, extra witnesses and dedicated capacity pay for the network. Witnessed reads Free On the hosted witness, rate-limited. Witnessed writes 2¢ Per call that changes something: POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE. Two-witness receipts +1¢ For high-value actions, once a second independent operator is live. Design-partner pilot $10,000 60 days. Setup, 250,000 witnessed actions and an evidence report your insurer can read. Dedicated or self-hosted witness Talk to us Your own witness key and capacity, with more than one witness for high-value actions. Security ## Built so you don’t have to trust us. The verifier needs the witness’s public key and the public web certificate roots. It never calls Histor, so a receipt keeps working even if Histor is gone. ### Two trust anchors A compressed secp256k1 witness key and the public web PKI. Nothing else. ### Secrets stay put Credentials for writes live on the server. Disclosure is fail-closed: a field that contains a credential cannot be revealed. ### Public targets only The witness resolves names itself and refuses loopback, private and cloud-metadata addresses. ### Open protocol Receipts are TLSNotary presentations. Signed statements are being mapped to COSE for IETF SCITT transparency services. ### Where things stand Updated 1 October 2026 Forge-at-birth proof Working Runs against the live api.weather.gov feed. 3 of 3 rounds behave as expected. histor CLI Built witness, fetch, verify. GET and writes, MPC and proxy modes, 20 unit tests passing. MCP server Built stdio and Streamable HTTP. Private beta. Hosted witness Built, not live Container built and tested. Its public key is published here the day it goes live. Second, independent witness operator Planned Until then, hosted receipts are labeled Histor-attested. Hardware-backed witness tier Planned Found a security issue? Email founder@verdict.systems with “Histor security” in the subject. Pilot access ## Bring us the agent action you most need to prove. Design-partner pilots run 60 days. We set up the witness, run your agents’ calls through it, and hand you a report your risk team or insurer can check on their own. Nothing here is for sale and nothing is ranked by quality. Does HISTOR tell me a server is safe? No, and it never will. It tells you what a server advertised, whether that changed, and which published patterns matched the text. Whether to trust the server is your decision — HISTOR makes sure you decide on the same facts as everyone else. Why are so many servers "not observed"? Most remote MCP endpoints require a login (they answer 401 to anyone without a key), some use the legacy SSE transport or need per-user values in the URL, and some are simply down. They stay on the list with the reason, so the numbers never hide them. How do I check a server I already use? Open the Check tab, paste the server's endpoint and the tools/list result your client received, and press Check. You get back, signed, whether HISTOR observed the same definitions — or different ones, or an older set. How do I get a badge for my server? Find your endpoint on the Servers tab, open it, and copy the Markdown snippet under the facts. The badge shows the date your definitions were pinned or last changed, and links to the full history. Why should I trust HISTOR itself? You do not have to. Every label and every tree head is signed with one published key; the Log tab proves in your browser that the log only grew; and the command-line auditor does the same from any machine. What remains is that one operator runs it today — a second, independent observer is the next step. What does it cost? Looking things up, the badges, the feed and /check are free. HISTOR also offers histor.check@v1 to the AIMarket Hub, so agents can reach it through the market. I run an MCP server. What does HISTOR send it, and how do I opt out? Once a day: initialize, notifications/initialized and tools/list — never a tool call, never a redirect followed, at most two connections per host, from a User-Agent that starts with histor/. To be left out, open an issue on the histor repository with your endpoint or host; it is then listed as not observed (operator-opt-out), with the reason, rather than silently dropped.
